claims.statement: `Dispatcher.on_message` is the ingest entry point for already-parsed messages: it awaits `IngestPipeline.run` inline, returns immediately when the result carries no message or no decision, notes a `relevance_gate` candidate with `ParticipationTrigger` instead of admitting it, and otherwise spawns an `EngagementRequest` into `EngagementPipeline.run`; it lives in `nora.app` because `nora.ingest` and `nora.engagement` are sibling packages that may not import each other.

Parsing and normalization happen inside each platform adapter's `listen()` loop, not in ingest: `PlatformAdapter` deliberately has no `parse()`, and an adapter drops any event that parses to `None` (Signal: a DM, a sync message, a self-send, an empty body; WhatsApp: a non-message event, `from_me`, a broadcast JID, an empty turn) before `on_message` is ever called.

`IngestPipeline` only sequences stage calls and assembles `IngestResult`; every branch belongs to the stage that owns it under `nora/ingest/stages/`, where each module exposes exactly one public `async def run(...)`.

The ordinary-message stage order is fixed: room scope, identity, media custody, external file links, quote target, the audit write, the stimulus, the spawned Honcho feed, the engage gate, then the sender gate — with custody before the record and the stimulus immediately after it.

The room gate runs before any write, so a conversation the operator has not allowlisted (or a DM from somebody absent from `identity.toml`) leaves no audit row at all, and the refusal is counted on `nora_denied_conversations_total`; the sender half of the grant is enforced later, after the audit, so an unrecognised sender in an allowed room stays discoverable via `nora persons pending`.

A failed audit write drops the message instead of raising: `stages/audit.py` catches the exception, logs it, increments `nora_errors_total{stage="ambient"}`, and returns `None`, because ingest runs on the listener's await path and a raise would stop ingest for every conversation on that adapter.

Identity resolution runs before the audit write so the resolved `person_id` lands in that single INSERT — `Persons.resolve` is two dict lookups on a startup-built frozen mapping, so nothing fallible moves ahead of the record, and a second UPDATE per message would contend for the single WAL writer. An unmapped sender is an expected outcome that resolves to `None`, ingest continues, and it is counted on `nora_unmapped_senders_total`.

Media custody runs inline ahead of the audit write so the body's handle and the blob backing it are committed by one INSERT; spawning the copy would write a promise of custody before the bytes existed, which is the A9 violation the stage exists to prevent.

Media custody is a wiring state, not a content branch: with `media_sources` or `blobs` absent every attachment is counted `nora_media_custody_total{status="not_configured"}` and the message is still recorded with a bare placeholder, while custody wired without a fetcher for that platform counts `not_supported` — two distinct operator problems with two labels.

Voice-note transcription is a separate wiring state from custody: when a `transcriber` is supplied, voice notes only are transcribed inline during custody and the transcript is written to `media_objects.content` (joined at render, not baked into the body), with the outcome counted on `nora_speech_transcriptions_total`; a failed transcription keeps the bare handle rather than dropping the note or inventing words.

Media comprehension is a third, spawned wiring state: when a `MediaComprehension` is supplied, each held blob with a handle is scheduled for one model read off the ingest path, landing title/description/content in `media_objects` and feeding Honcho under the sender's peer, with three outcomes `ok` / `nothing_found` / `unavailable`; with it absent every attachment keeps its bare handle and nothing is model-read, but the synchronously captured voice transcript is still written.

The ingest body carries only a closed-set label and a content hash per attachment; a description or transcript is stored in `media_objects` and selected by each consumer at render time, which is why the `scan_identifiers` egress screen runs on every render rather than once at store time.

Shared file links become `ExternalFileRef`s in the record with no network call and no configuration: `stages/external_files.py` only reads the body, and the refs land in `messages.external_files_json` in the same INSERT as the row.

`stages/quote_target.py` rewrites a Signal reply's `quoted_ts` from the timestamp of the revision the replier saw to the original message's `ts` before the audit write, so every downstream reader resolves the parent; it runs on Signal only, an exact match always wins, and a failed lookup leaves the quote as sent rather than dropping the message.

The Honcho feed is spawned, never awaited, and skipped entirely for an unmapped sender; file links are fed as handles rather than URLs, and an edit is fed as a framed correction quoting the version it first said so the deriver reads it as a change rather than a second statement.

The engage gate degrades closed: any exception from `EngagePolicy.should_engage` is logged, counted `nora_errors_total{stage="engage_gate"}`, and becomes `EngageDecision(engage=False, reason="policy_error")` rather than propagating and taking the listener down over a classifier outage.

`IngestOutcome` is a closed `Literal` of sixteen values that derives the `nora_ingest_outcomes_total` label vocabulary via `get_args`, treats an exception as not-an-ending because the span already stamps the exception type, and logs but still records an undeclared outcome because mypy does not reach `nora/ingest`.

The outcome counter is the live reporting instrument and the span attribute is latent by design: an ingest contains no model call, so the ingest trace is declared `plumbing` at span start and dropped by the sampler, while `nora_ingest_outcomes_total{platform, conversation_type, outcome}` carries what it would have said.

The ingest root span carries only room-scoped or structural facts — `nora.platform`, `nora.conversation_id`, `nora.conversation_type`, `nora.attachments`, plus a `nora.person_known` bool and the gate's `nora.engage_reason` — never a sender id, display name, message body or coordinate.

Neither half of the observation reporting is load-bearing: `annotate` is guarded inside `nora.obs.tracing`, and the counter increment in `_outcome` is wrapped in its own try/except, because an ingest runs on the listener's await path and an exception from an observation would stop ingest for every conversation on the adapter.

`IngestResult.message` is `None` in exactly two message-path cases — the room is not allowlisted, or the audit write failed — plus every branch that writes no message at all; a message that got past the audit is always paired with a decision, even for an unmapped sender or a policy error.

An edit takes its own path immediately after the room gate: `stages/edit_target.py` answers found / `edit_orphaned` / `edit_stale` / `edit_refused` before anything is written, treating a withdrawn (hidden) original as orphaned, and comparing authorship on the platform id first and the resolved person second.

An edit's attachments are given back the handles Nora already holds instead of being re-fetched, and custody only runs when the positional match cannot be trusted (differing counts, or a bare placeholder gap in the original).

`stages/edit_record.py` decides "unchanged" on the post-custody text and mentions, so a Discord link-preview update or a bridge redelivery is not mistaken for an edit; an unchanged-but-newer edit is still written (a Signal client addresses its next edit by that timestamp) while only a true duplicate writes nothing, and a failed write drops the edit without raising.

`stages/edit_gate.py` runs the engage policy twice — on the edit and on the version it replaced — and engages only when the first says yes and the second says no, so an added @-mention is a turn while a typo fix on an already-tagged message is not; it clears `relevance_gate` unconditionally because an edit is not new room activity.

A turn opened by an edit is answered as the ORIGINAL message — its timestamp and its platform message handle — because that is the message the room sees and what a reaction or threaded reply must point at.

A reaction or a delete becomes no `messages` row, no transcript line, no Honcho feed and no turn: `stages/touch.py` finds the target, records the item beside it in `message_reaction` / `message_delete`, hides the target on a delete, refuses an author-only (Signal) delete naming somebody else's message, and drops an orphan without a target on record.

The stimulus stage appends exactly one row per recorded person-authored item — message, changed edit, reaction, delete — after the Record write it names, with `ref` pointing at `<table>:<row_id>` and cues attached; Nora's own items raise none, and a reply to her message inside `reply_quiet_seconds` is recorded with `waits` so it never starts a wake by itself.

The stimulus stage is off unless `[cognition] enabled` wires it: with `stimulus_wiring = None` nothing is written and the stage's span is never opened, and even when wired the whole body is guarded with a timeout so a failure costs lateness only, never the already-recorded item.
`nora_messages_total` is incremented once per message and once per edit, while a reaction or a delete is counted only on `nora_ingest_outcomes_total` because neither is a message.

The outcome vocabulary is pinned in both directions by tests that read `get_args` off `IngestOutcome` and the rendered counter rather than a hand-copied list, and a further test asserts that none of the counter's three labels can carry an identifier, with a positive control proving the screen fires on a phone number.

The integration harness reproduces production's parse-then-dispatch boundary rather than bypassing it: `_HandlerView.on_event` calls `parse_event`, drops a `None` result, and then calls `Dispatcher.on_message`, because `IngestPipeline` accepts no raw dicts.

The message path is not the only ingest path that reaches an engagement gate: a changed edit runs `edit_gate` and the sender gate, counts `edit_engaged` or `edit_recorded`, and returns an `IngestResult` whose `message` is the ORIGINAL message (its timestamp and platform message id, `answered_as`) paired with the decision, so `Dispatcher.on_message` can spawn a turn for an edit; only the touch path's endings, the refused/orphaned/stale edit targets and the unchanged-edit endings return `IngestResult(message=None, decision=None)`.

The pipeline maps two distinct `edit_record` results onto the single outcome label `edit_unchanged`: `recorded_unchanged` (a newer style-only edit, which does write one `message_edit` row so the next edit's timestamp chain survives, but raises no stimulus, feeds no Honcho correction and opens no turn) and `edit_unchanged` (a true duplicate, which writes nothing), so a non-zero count on that label does not mean the room saw no change, nor that nothing was written.
